Selection rationale 
Article — No separate article-choice rationale is recorded. 
Model — The researcher selected this published North Sea 1991 Rpath snapshot on 
14/10/2026 because its static mass-balance checks pass. Recorded limitations include its 
difference from the native EwE Key Run, source routing restrictions and loader 
departures. Numerical readiness and researcher approval were not established. 
Model extraction 
Source reconciliation and round-trip checks support the deposited Rpath port. Missing source 
inputs were completed only from deposited outputs: biomass for 8 groups, Q/B for 11 and EE 
for 61. Static source budgets balance, with five P/Q range warnings. 
The repaired shared loader retains published phytoplankton routing, explicit zero detritus -
fate rows, source TL and catch. Four missing import-diet cells for nonfeeding groups use a 
documented structural-zero convention. No source parameters or diets were changed. 
Published fleet discards return 0.49945 t/km²/year to Discards (69). Accounting now includes 
their donor PPR once and separates internal returns from external removals. The former 
negative detritus coefficients and large PP-budget failure disappear under the stated runtime 
assumptions.

Comparison of the two candidates 
Recommend retaining ICES North Sea 1991 as the selected candidate for further validation. The repaired 
implementation now converges with finite, nonnegative results and a closed PP budget in all three methods, 
and its declared domain covers substantially more of LME_022 than Scotland. This supersedes the provisional 
Scotland preference based on the faulty ICES runtime. ICES still has material sensitivity warnings, runtime 
closure assumptions, no exact-model catch mapping and no recovered native Key Run database; it is not yet 
ready for an approved regional PPR estimate.
